detailedExplanation: Verified against The Tiffin Girls’ School Year 9 Physics Curriculum Outline 2026–27 and aligned to AQA GCSE Physics 8463.

When a gas is heated, the average kinetic energy and speed of its particles increase. At fixed volume, faster particles collide with the container walls more frequently and with greater changes of momentum.
The increased collision rate and force of collisions raise the gas pressure when the volume is fixed.
Cooling has the opposite effect: particle speeds and average kinetic energy fall, so the pressure decreases if the volume remains unchanged.

When temperature relationships are treated quantitatively beyond simple GCSE explanation, absolute temperature in kelvin is required. For Year 9 questions here, focus first on the particle explanation and experimental controls.
examTips: Use a collision explanation: hotter → faster particles → more frequent/harder wall collisions → higher pressure.
